# Copilot Instructions for pika-skills

## Project mission

This project — **Inclusive Game Day** — is a **free, non-commercial, open-source** resource dedicated to making tabletop and group games genuinely accessible, especially for people with invisible disabilities, sensory needs, neurodivergence, chronic illness, and any condition that can make participation difficult.

All code, content, and documentation generated for this repository must reflect that mission.

---

## Non-commercial requirement

- This project has **no revenue model** of any kind.
- Do **not** generate content that implies, promotes, or introduces:
  - Paid tiers, premium features, or paywalls
  - Affiliate links or referral schemes
  - Sponsored content or brand partnerships
  - Advertising, tracking pixels, or analytics
  - Upsell or conversion-funnel language
- All resources must be and remain **freely available** to everyone.

---

## Netlify Open Source Plan eligibility

This site is hosted under **Netlify's Open Source Plan**.

To preserve eligibility, all generated content must:

- Keep the **Netlify credit visible** on the main page (`index.html`). The footer must contain a plainly visible attribution such as:
  > "This site is powered by [Netlify](https://www.netlify.com/)."
- Never remove, hide, or obscure the Netlify attribution.
- Not introduce any commercial monetisation (ads, paid plans, sponsored links) that would disqualify the project from the Open Source Plan.
- Not represent this as a commercial or for-profit project.

---

## Disability inclusion and accessibility standards

This project explicitly serves people with **invisible disabilities** and sensory needs.

- Write all user-facing copy in **plain, clear language** — avoid jargon, idioms, and metaphors that may confuse neurodiverse readers.
- Do not require visible proof of disability or impose gatekeeping language.
- All HTML contributions must include appropriate `aria-*` attributes, semantic elements, and `alt` text for images.
- Do not use colour as the sole means of conveying information.
- Avoid flashing animations or auto-playing media.
- Prefer high-contrast colour combinations and readable font sizes.

---

## Tone and language rules

- **Do use:** community-oriented, welcoming, plain-English, practical, educational, empowering.
- **Do not use:** sales language, urgency cues ("Buy now", "Limited offer"), client/customer framing, corporate voice, or affiliate-style calls to action.
- Descriptions of features should explain **how they help people**, not how they benefit a business.

---

## Homepage (`index.html`) guidelines

- Keep the homepage **clear, simple, and accessible** — it is the primary public face of the project.
- The page must immediately communicate:
  1. What the project is (free, open-source, accessible games resource)
  2. Who it is for (people with disabilities, sensory needs, and access requirements)
  3. That it is non-commercial (no paywalls, no ads, no data collection)
- Do not add hero images, carousels, or decorative elements that add cognitive or sensory load without a clear accessibility benefit.
- Retain the existing badge/callout pattern that shows "Non-Commercial · Public Interest · Open Source".

---

## Contribution and code quality

- Generated code must be consistent with the existing MIT-licensed codebase.
- Do not introduce new third-party dependencies without a clear accessibility or public-interest justification.
- Do not add analytics, telemetry, cookie banners, or any tracking code.
- Follow semantic HTML5 practices and keep CSS minimal and readable.
